impact_statement: The stack-exhaustion denial of service (CVE-2026-93687, GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) requires evaluating deeply nested, attacker-controlled brace-expansion patterns. The braces maintainer considers the advisory only exploitable when an application passes user-supplied patterns to braces: hitting a nesting depth of 5,000 already requires more than 10,000 characters of input, and input-length limits (maxLength) are a sufficient, already-supported mitigation (https://github.com/micromatch/braces/issues/70). In N|Solid, braces reaches the runtime only inside the ncm-ng agent through fast-glob -> micromatch -> braces, and every glob pattern ncm-ng evaluates is hardcoded (workers/certifyNG/install-scripts.js and workers/general/getLocalModuleFilePaths.js match fixed patterns such as '**/*.js' under the user's own working directory), so adversarial brace patterns cannot reach braces through N|Solid. braces has no patched release (every version <= 3.0.3 is affected), so an exemption is the only available remediation. npm audit surfaces this single advisory in deps/ncm-ng as three findings (braces directly, plus the micromatch and fast-glob chain findings), tracked in https://github.com/nodesource/nsolid-dependency-vuln-assessments/issues/2934, https://github.com/nodesource/nsolid-dependency-vuln-assessments/issues/2935 and https://github.com/nodesource/nsolid-dependency-vuln-assessments/issues/2936.

action_statement: Upstream fixes backported to the minimatch copies bundled with npm and with Node.js, and to the copy inlined in npm's glob 13.0.6 bundles: at optimizationLevel 2, the **/.. split pass throws a RangeError rather than make more than braceExpandMax patterns or add more than 1,000,000 path portions, and sets of more than 1000 patterns are not deduplicated. Upstream fixes: https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/commit/77a0f5c4b80bdc641c3c930a1d9edf5ad2db57f8 and https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/pull/336

impact_statement: The flaw is in how glob handles an AbortSignal: after an aborted walk rejects, glob keeps reading directories. npm never passes a signal to glob (its callers are the help and help-search commands, @npmcli/map-workspaces, @npmcli/package-json and cacache), so the affected abort branches never run.

This CVE is in HdrHistogram's Java implementation (org.HdrHistogram, through 2.2.2). N|Solid bundles HdrHistogram_c, the separate C implementation in deps/histogram, which shares none of the affected code.
